questions.question: CSS custom properties (variables) are declared as:
questions.explanation: Custom properties use the --name syntax. $ is Sass; var() is how you READ a variable, not declare it.

questions.question: You consume a variable with:
questions.explanation: var(--name) reads the custom property. You can supply a fallback: var(--x, #000).

questions.question: A key advantage of CSS variables over preprocessor vars is:

options.text: They are runtime/live — can change via JS and respond to media queries/state

questions.explanation: CSS vars are live in the browser: update via element.style or :root, animate, and react to themes — unlike static preprocessor constants.

questions.question: Defining --brand on :root makes it:
questions.explanation: :root is the document root; a variable declared there is inherited everywhere — the standard place for theme tokens.

questions.question: CSS variables CASCADE and are:

options.text: Inherited — a child inherits the value from its parent unless overridden

questions.explanation: Custom properties inherit like color/font-family. This enables theming: set --brand on a container, all descendants use it.

questions.question: You can update a CSS variable from JavaScript via:
questions.explanation: setProperty('--name', value) updates a custom property live — great for themes, sliders, and dynamic styling.

questions.question: A common use for CSS variables is:

options.text: Centralized design tokens (colors, spacing, radii) and theming (light/dark)

questions.explanation: Tokens + theming are the canonical use: switch a few root vars to re-skin the whole app (incl. dark mode).

questions.question: A fallback value is written as:
questions.explanation: The second argument to var() is the fallback used when the variable is not defined (or invalid).
